title: fix(core, fields): refuse an empty or non-string `$icontains` comparand, and stop the builder emitting it (objectui#8748)
body:
Fixes #8748

`ValueDataSource` answered an empty `$icontains` / `icontains` comparand with **every row and not one console line**, and evaluated a non-string comparand after a `String()` coercion nobody wrote. `@objectstack/spec`'s `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` carries both shapes as REJECTION rows. This PR refuses both, in both dialects, and — in the same change — stops `FilterConditionField` emitting the shape.

## Re-measured on current `main` before any edit

The card's readings were taken on `da5e4f69`; `main` is now `0f5cadfa1` (objectui#8513 / PR #8771 landed `$and` / `$or` execution in this very file since). All three probe rows reproduced, over the real `ValueDataSource` and `@objectstack/spec`'s own `FILTER_TEXT_ROWS`, both dialects:

| probe | on `0f5cadfa1` | after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `{ name: { $icontains: '' } }` | `["1","2","3","4","5","6","7","8","9"]`, console `[]` | `[]` + 1 refusal naming `$icontains` |
| `['name','icontains','']` | `["1","2","3","4","5","6","7","8","9"]`, console `[]` | `[]` + 1 refusal naming `icontains` |
| `{ name: { $icontains: 42 }}` | `[]` via `String(42)`, console `[]` | `[]` + 1 refusal naming `$icontains` |
| **live control** `{ name: { $icontains: 'acme' }}` | `["1","2"]`, console `[]` | `["1","2"]`, console `[]` — unchanged |
| **lit control** `[]` (no filter) | all nine | all nine — unchanged |

## The two halves, and why neither ships alone

**Matcher (`@object-ui/core`).** The `icontains` and `$icontains` arms now check the comparand before folding: anything that is not a NON-EMPTY STRING excludes the row and drains one console refusal naming the operator and the field.

This is objectui#7349's mechanism — **exclude the row and log it, not throw.** The throwing envelope belongs to the wire-side sibling `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, which is deciding whether to send a query at all; this matcher is deciding about one row. Whether this face should carry the throwing envelope is objectui#8600 Q1 and stays closed with it.

**Producer (`@object-ui/fields`).** `condToMongo` emitted `{ [field]: { $icontains: value } }` verbatim, and the only drop on that path was the missing-FIELD guard (`filterGroupToMongo` discards null fragments and nothing else). A builder row with the operator chosen and the value box still empty therefore authored exactly the refused filter. It is now dropped, for the five free-text operators (`contains`, `containsCaseInsensitive`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`) on `undefined` / `null` / `''`.

⚠️ That half is what makes the refusal safe at the SEAM — refusing in the matcher alone flips a half-built builder row from "every row" to "no rows", the outcome `ValueDataSource`'s own `$exists` docblock names as the one worse than the bug. ⚠️ But the drop alone was not safe in the UI, and the contract review measured it: this widget is a **controlled round-trip**, so the row projected from the stored criteria deleted itself the moment the operator was switched. That is F1 below, and it is fixed in this PR — the rows are now local state. The value-less operators (`isNull` / `exists` / `isEmpty` and their negations) read no comparand and are untouched; so is `equals ''`, which is a real predicate.

The producer half also moves **stored criteria** for the four sibling operators it covers: `contains ''` / `startsWith ''` / `endsWith ''` used to store a predicate the server evaluates as "the value is a string", and `notContains ''` stored its complement, "the value is not a string". All four now store no fragment at all, so a rule whose only row was one of them saves as empty criteria and is refused on save (objectstack#3896) rather than sharing by storage class. Criteria already stored keep their fragment and keep evaluating as they did.

## Scope held

- **The sibling positive operators are deliberately NOT widened by analogy.** `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` declares the empty-comparand refusal for `$icontains` and for no other operator, so `$contains ''` keeps the answer it has always given. The asymmetry is pinned as its own case so the next reader sees a scope boundary rather than an oversight.
- **`FILTER_TEXT_CASES` enrolment is not here** (objectui#8600, closed). Measured on the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0: the table carries **19** cases, below the 24-case reopen threshold.
- **The `$options` short-circuit does not ride along.** Measured: `{ name: { $regex: 'x', $options: 'i' } }` drains one refusal naming `$regex` only. That short-circuit is `matchesFilter`'s per-operator `return false`, a different site from the two comparand arms this PR touches — so it is not on the same lines, and per the card it stays with objectui#8600's reopen note.
- Nothing touched on the wire-side `data-objectstack` matcher.

## Patch round — contract review CHANGES REQUIRED

Answering the audit-tier contract review at https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/8791#issuecomment-5598917902 (head `598dd6ef96`). Implemented by the director seat's `os-dev` round, session `session_017Js5kTpTtxieBjPyScgxJ3`; the card's existing `Claim:` and assignee stand and were not touched.

| item | disposition |
| --- | --- |
| **F1** (blocking) — the producer drop deletes the builder row | **Fixed.** `FilterConditionField` holds the `BuilderGroup` as local state, seeded from the parsed criteria and re-seeded only when the incoming criteria stops being what those rows emit (an outside change). The drop stays at emission. New render-level pin, and an ablation that reproduces the vanishing row. |
| **F2** (blocking) — the adapters README refusal table is incomplete | **Fixed.** The comparand-shape row is in the table, in the verdict's wording, plus one clause on the `$icontains` paragraph above it. |
| **F3** — the changeset's Migration covers only the matcher | **Fixed.** The four sibling operators' before→after on STORED criteria is now stated in the changeset and in the section above. |
| **F4** — a second "row finished" rule beside `isFilterValueComplete` | **Fixed by saying so.** The `TEXT_COMPARAND_OPERATORS` docblock now states why the two diverge (`equals ''` is a real predicate here) and why composing the two is not adopted: it would bind this drop to a helper marked `@internal` in another package, whose vocabulary is the dropdown's rather than the spec's. |
| **F5** — `JSON.stringify` in the refusal message throws on a BigInt or a cyclic comparand | **Fixed, and the class with it.** One `describeComparand` helper, used by BOTH sites — the new text-comparand refusal and the pre-existing `$field` one at the same shape the verdict cites as the idiom. Output is byte-identical for every input that did not throw. Pinned. |
| **F6** — the AST refusal names `icontains`, not `$icontains` | **Kept as it is**, which is what the verdict allows ("naming what the author wrote is defensible; note only"). Naming the token the author typed is what makes the message actionable at the AST door, and `FILTER_TEXT_CASES`' `mustMention` is satisfied by the `$` dialect's own arm. |
| **F7** — report accuracy | The claim about the producer half is corrected above; the round's report on the card states the measured UI outcome rather than the seam-level one. |

## Tests

Pinned as the card asks: the two `ValueDataSource` files keep their existing lit controls, every new row asserts the excluded row set **and** the console refusal, and each row has a live control beside it.

- `ValueDataSource.textOperatorCase.test.ts` — the EMPTY comparand, both dialects, plus the dialect-agreement case, plus the untouched-`$contains` boundary.
- `ValueDataSource.nonStringStoredValue.test.ts` — the non-string COMPARAND, both dialects. ⚠️ Pinned on the refusal becoming observable, never on "`42` and `'42'` agree" — that assertion passes before the fix too. This fixture discriminates where the card's did not: `{ score: { $icontains: 5 } }` used to return `['s5']` through the coercion and now returns `[]` with a named refusal, while the string comparand `'5'` still returns `['s5']`.
- `FilterConditionField.operators.test.ts` — the producer drop, with the non-empty comparand, the value-less operators and `equals ''` as live controls.
- `FilterConditionField.builderRows-8748.test.tsx` — **new in the patch round**, and the only level that can see F1: the widget rendered inside a controlled parent that stores what it emits. Add a row, switch to `containsCaseInsensitive`, and the row is still on screen with the operator shown and the value box empty while the emitted criteria is `''`; type `acme` and it emits `{"name":{"$icontains":"acme"}}`. Two guards ride with it — a stored `{ name: { $icontains: 'x' } }` still seeds the rows and emits nothing on mount, and an outside change to the stored value still replaces them — so a widget that merely IGNORED its incoming value would fail the suite rather than pass it.

**Ablation — three legs, each mutation proven on disk (git blob hash before/after), each classified per test from vitest's JSON reporter, each restored to `HEAD` and the restore proven by an empty `git diff HEAD`:**

| leg mutated back to pre-card form | classified result |
|---|---|
| `$icontains` arm (`@object-ui/core`) | 4 failed / 37 passed — the 4 `$`-dialect rows; AST rows and every control stayed green |
| `icontains` arm (`@object-ui/core`) | 3 failed / 38 passed — the 3 AST rows |
| `condToMongo` drop (`@object-ui/fields`) | 15 failed / 51 passed — all 15 producer rows; the controls stayed green |

**Ablation — patch round, two more legs, same discipline** (mutation proven on disk by git blob hash before/after, classified per test from vitest's JSON reporter, restored with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` under a trap on absolute paths, restore proven by hash equality with the HEAD blob AND an empty `git diff HEAD`; the fix was committed first, so `HEAD` carried the implementation). Neither leg needs a rebuild: both suites reach their subject through a RELATIVE import of the source file, not through a package `exports` entry, so nothing is read out of `dist/`.

| leg mutated back | classified result |
| --- | --- |
| the local row state (`value={localGroup}` back to the projection `value={group ?? EMPTY_GROUP}`) | **2 failed / 2 passed** — exactly the two F1 tests, and they fail with `TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an accessible element with the role "combobox"`: the row is GONE, which is the defect in its own words. The seed guard and the outside-change guard stayed green |
| `describeComparand(target)` back to `JSON.stringify(target) ?? String(target)` | **1 failed / 22 passed** — the new BigInt / cyclic comparand pin, alone |

Commands run in the FIRST round, on `598dd6ef9` (every build/test through the container's shared verify lock; verdict lines quoted, never a bare `$?`):

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the four pinned files → `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 107 passed (107)`; `VERDICT command-exit 0`
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/fields test` → core `134 passed (134)` / `2855 passed (2855)`, fields `149 passed (149)` / `2564 passed (2564)`; `VERDICT command-exit 0`
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/core^...' --filter '@object-ui/fields^...' build` → 9 packages `Done`; `VERDICT command-exit 0`
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` → both `Done` (each is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the test files are covered too); `VERDICT command-exit 0`

Gates run locally, each printing a non-zero scanned population rather than a silent no-op: `check:control-bytes` (6986 files), `check:spec-symbols` (1366 files / 5050 export names), `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:self-import` — all OK. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the six changed paths: `NOT GOVERNED`, and the lit control (the same command shape with `AGENTS.md` appended) fires `⛔ GOVERNED`, so that zero is a reading. Plus a control-byte self-scan over the changed files.

Commands run in the PATCH round, on `93291f45f` — the merge of `origin/main` into this branch, which is also where every number below was taken (the branch was 30 commits behind; nothing on main touched `ValueDataSource`, `FilterConditionField` or `filter-builder`, and the two overlapping files are `DateField.tsx` / `FormulaField.tsx` in the same package, which is why the fields suite is re-run on the merge result):

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/core^...' --filter '@object-ui/fields^...' build` → 9 packages `Done`; `VERDICT command-exit 0`
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` → both `Done`; `VERDICT command-exit 0`. Each is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and the new `.test.tsx` is genuinely IN that program — `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` names it among the 1588 files it compiles, so this is a reading and not a NOT-MEASURED
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/fields test` → core `Test Files 134 passed (134)` / `Tests 2856 passed (2856)`, fields `Test Files 153 passed (153)` / `Tests 2623 passed (2623)`; `VERDICT command-exit 0`
- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the new file alone → `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 4 passed (4)`; `VERDICT command-exit 0`

Gates re-run locally on the merged head, each printing a non-zero scanned population rather than a silent no-op: `check:control-bytes` (7043 files), `check:vi-mock-specifiers` / `check:vi-mock-inherit` (4659 files, 2901 test-named), `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:self-import`, `check:spec-symbols` (1366 sources + 184 doc pages), `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` (46 packages, 42/42 compile their tests) — all exit 0. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over this PR's eight changed paths: `NOT GOVERNED`, and the lit control (the same command with `AGENTS.md` appended) fires the governed refusal, so that zero is a reading. Plus a control-byte self-scan over the changed files with the raw-byte regex.

⚠️ `check:readme-exports` is **NOT MEASURED** here, not green and not red. Its own workflow builds every package first (`turbo run build --filter='./packages/*'`) and this container built only the core/fields dependency closure, so the gate reported `the population COLLAPSED -- this run proves nothing` over 27 unbuilt packages. Every path it named is a `plugin-*` README; it named none of this PR's files, and the README this PR edits is `packages/core/src/adapters/README.md`, which is not one of the `packages/PKG/README.md` files that gate reads. It is CI's run.

**Declared narrowing — eslint.** Run on this PR's changed files rather than repo-wide; the repo-wide scan is CI's. Re-measured at the final commit `93291f45f`: population **4657** files (read from eslint's own config — every git-tracked file with a lintable extension, 4659, minus everything `isPathIgnored` rejects), **6** files linted (count read from `--format json`), **0 errors**, 93 warnings (`--max-warnings` is deliberately unset in `lint.yml`): 86 `no-explicit-any`, 4 `react-refresh/only-export-components`, 3 `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`. ⚠️ One of those three is NEW — the re-seed effect this patch round adds. It is the third instance in this same file of a category the file already carried twice (`setFields(null)` and `setRawMode(true)`), and it is deliberate: the alternative, adjusting the state during render, cannot be made to converge when a stored criteria does not round-trip through the builder (a legacy `$ncontains` spelling reads back as `notContains` and emits `$notContains`), and React throws on that rather than settling. The effect form bails out on an identical value instead. Invariance: `eslint.config.js` extends `tseslint.configs.recommended` with no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService` and no `*TypeChecked` config — type-aware linting is not enabled, so every verdict is a function of a file's own text plus the config, and this diff changes neither the config nor any of the other 4623 files. The narrowing therefore excludes nothing.

## Carriers

**`Clause-②: yes`** — the matcher half moves the accept set of a published adapter. `needs:contract-review` is hung on this PR; changeset **`minor`** for `@object-ui/core` and `@object-ui/fields`.

⚠️ `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is measured unavailable (429, `req_011CesRvRDtifao1i75vuaXb`, ~06:57Z). Per objectui#8069 comment 5594065532 that gates the **review**, not the construction. This PR is therefore **expected to sit as a draft**: ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ no auto-merge, ⛔ not flipped ready — the contract review is owed on this diff first, and that is the PM seat's call.

## 验收备注

Noted while reading, deliberately **not** filed and **not** fixed here:

- `$contains` / `$startsWith` / `$endsWith` with an empty comparand still evaluate (all string-valued rows / none). Not a contract violation — `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` declares the refusal for `$icontains` alone — so there is nothing to file against this repo. The PR that has to answer it is objectui#8600's reopen, which enrols this face in the whole table; it touches exactly these arms. Pinned here as a boundary case so the asymmetry cannot be read as an oversight.
- The `$options` short-circuit is re-measured and unchanged (see Scope held). It stays with objectui#8600's reopen note, as the card directs.

Added in the patch round, and likewise not filed:

- The AST-door refusal names `icontains` and the `$`-door one names `$icontains`, because each names the token its author wrote. Contract review F6 records this as defensible and note-only, so it is left alone; the spec's `mustMention` is satisfied on the `$` side by that side's own arm.
- `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` now has three instances in `FilterConditionField.tsx` where it had two. Reasoned above under the eslint narrowing, not filed: the rule is a warning here, the file already carried the category, and the render-phase alternative is the one that can fail to converge.

Patch round implemented by the director seat's `os-dev`, session `session_017Js5kTpTtxieBjPyScgxJ3`, on the branch's existing claim — no second `Claim:` was posted, the assignee was not written, and no label or draft state was touched. Attribution is written here as prose because a `PATCH` to this body rewrites the footer.
